newsitem.title: UK: Contact group says Serbs must cooperate in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Contact group says Serbs must cooperate in Bosnia.

text.p: The five-nation "contact group" on Thursday told Bosnian Serbs they had to start cooperating with the newly-elected Bosnian presidency or they would put at risk international funds designed to help rebuild the country.
The group, which brings together the United States, Russia, France, Germany and Britain, said in a statement issued in London than further obstruction was just not "acceptable".
"The contact group...notes the reconstruction of Bosnia remains a key priority and that considerable resources are available for all parts of Bosnia.

"But the international community's willingness and ability to distribute these resources to all communities in Bosnia will depend on the attitude and support of those communities to the new central institutions," the statement said.
The contact group statement echoed a message given by British Foreign Office minister Sir Nicholas Bonsor directly to the Bosnian Serb leadership on Thursday.
Bonsor told a news conference in Sarajevo he had told Bosnian Serb presidency member Momcilo Krajisnik of the importance of the country's three-man presidency and its joint national assembly.

Krajisnik and the Serb deputies stayed away from the first National Assembly session on Saturday, arguing that there were insufficient guarantees for their safety, and objecting to an oath of alliegence to the Bosnian constitution.

Bonsor said: "I made it clear to him that unless the presidency progresses and unless the Republika Srpska (Bosnian Serb) representatives do cooperate fully in the process of getting this government in place then clearly the funds which the World Bank and other international institutions have set aside for them will not be forthcoming."
Bonsor, on a three-day visit to Bosnia, said Krajisnik had accepted the point and would do everything to ensure that the assembly did meet as soon as possible.

As well as urging Krajisnik to attend the next meeting of the joint presidency, the contact group said in its statement it also expected the commitment of all parties to municipal elections planned for November 23.
Although Krajisnik now appears to be backing off from confrontation, other Bosnian Serb leaders appear undeterred.

Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic has told the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, the body charged with supervising Bosnian elections, that the Serbs could call their own local elections according to their own rules.
